title: Update reference to iso 8601

labels.name: Spec-EPUB3
labels.description: The issue affects the core EPUB 3.X Recommendation

labels.name: Errata
labels.description: Item accepted as an official errata for one or several specs

labels.name: Change-Class-2
labels.description: Requested changes are of class 2 (per process)

body:
## Issue on the [EPUB 3.3](https://www.w3.org/TR/epub-33/) Recommendation

Section 5.5.3.2.4 The dc:date element

## Describe the problem 

I noticed we have a reference in that section to iso8601:2004 which in turn links to the withdrawn standard page: https://www.iso.org/standard/40874.html

## Describe the fix or new feature you propose

Change the reference to 8601-1:2019

We might also want to look at why we say dcterms:modified must be an xmlschema-2 conformant dateTime, even though it uses a pattern that also conforms to iso 8601. My guess is that reference was meant to match the package document schemas and the dc:date reference came later. It would probably be better to have both date formats reference the same standard.

title: Update conformance list to include wcag 2.2

labels.name: Spec-Accessibility
labels.description: The issue affects the EPUB Accessibility 1.X Recommendation

labels.name: Errata
labels.description: Item accepted as an official errata for one or several specs

labels.name: Change-Class-2
labels.description: Requested changes are of class 2 (per process)

body:
While updating the techniques document, it occurred to me that all our undated wcag2 references now point people to 2.2. Our list of conformance strings in the accessibility spec only shows values for 2.0 and 2.1, however.

Although the conformance strings adapt to new values, should we make 2.2 conformance explicit in the specification? It should only count as a category 2 change since we'd only be adding examples of the strings.

title: Nav doc semantics aren't required by the specification

labels.name: Spec-EPUB3
labels.description: The issue affects the core EPUB 3.X Recommendation

labels.name: Errata
labels.description: Item accepted as an official errata for one or several specs

labels.name: Change-Class-2
labels.description: Requested changes are of class 2 (per process)

body:
One of the things you stop seeing after a while, I guess, but despite calling the sections "The toc nav element" and "The page-list nav element", we don't appear to require any specific semantic be used on these nav elements. An epub:type attribute is required, but not a specific value.

The semantics are implied by the sections and the obviousness of the semantic names, of course, but that's not exactly sound spec writing. And the structure vocab mentions their intended uses in the usage details section for each, but that's also not normative.

It would be better if each of the toc, page-list, and, landmarks nav sections required those semantics in their respective epub:type attributes.

(On a side note, there's a typo in the first sentence of the page-list nav section. It says "The `page-list` element provides ..." but it should be "The `page-list nav` element provides ")

title: Remote resources not on web?

labels.name: Spec-EPUB3
labels.description: The issue affects the core EPUB 3.X Recommendation

labels.name: Errata
labels.description: Item accepted as an official errata for one or several specs

labels.name: Change-Class-2
labels.description: Requested changes are of class 2 (per process)

body:
I noticed the definition of remote resource is:

> remote resource
> A [publication resource](https://www.w3.org/TR/epub-33/#dfn-publication-resource) that is located outside of the [EPUB container](https://www.w3.org/TR/epub-33/#dfn-epub-container), typically, but not necessarily, on the web.

The "typically, but not necessarily, on the web" part looks like a relic from when we didn't ban the `file://` protocol in URLs, or is there some other non-web hosting that we support? The recommendation now is to use https for anything not in the container.

I think we can make the "web" part a parenthetical clarification:

> A [publication resource](https://www.w3.org/TR/epub-33/#dfn-publication-resource) that is located outside of the [EPUB container](https://www.w3.org/TR/epub-33/#dfn-epub-container) (i.e., on the web).

Or even just say: "A publication resource that is located on the web." It kind of stands to reason that a web-based resource can't also be in the container.

body:
[Section 3.6](https://www.w3.org/TR/epub-33/#sec-resource-locations) has a broken reference to RFC 7230:

> When resources have to be located outside the EPUB container, EPUB creators are RECOMMENDED to reference them via the secure https URI scheme [rfc7230]

(The use of URI looks fine here since it's defined in the rfc.)

title: URI mention without reference

labels.name: Spec-EPUB3
labels.description: The issue affects the core EPUB 3.X Recommendation

labels.name: Type-Editorial
labels.description: The issue does not affect conformance

labels.name: Errata
labels.description: Item accepted as an official errata for one or several specs

labels.name: Change-Class-2
labels.description: Requested changes are of class 2 (per process)

body:
[Section 5.5.3.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/epub-33/#sec-opf-dcidentifier) says:

> EPUB creators MAY specify additional identifiers. The identifiers should be fully qualified URIs.

But we dropped URI references during 3.3 in favour of URL.

I think this could be rewritten as:

> EPUB creators MAY specify additional identifiers. The identifiers should be [absolute-url strings](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#absolute-url-string) [url].

Since it's an informative recommendation, this change shouldn't rise above class 2, at least.

title: The formal/stable WebP specification

labels.name: Spec-EPUB3
labels.description: The issue affects the core EPUB 3.X Recommendation

labels.name: Errata
labels.description: Item accepted as an official errata for one or several specs

labels.name: Change-Class-2
labels.description: Requested changes are of class 2 (per process)

body:
It seems somewhat odd that the spec listed Google's developer page as a Normative reference for WebP.

Initially, this description was merged (https://github.com/w3c/epub-specs/pull/1347) with a warning about the instability of the spec, but the notes seems to have been removed (https://github.com/w3c/epub-specs/pull/1997) without much discussion since then.

Currently, the WebP specification is being developed by the IETF and is in [AUTH48](https://www.rfc-editor.org/auth48/rfc9403), the final stages of the publication queue.

While it will probably be a few more weeks before the WebP spec becomes [Infomational RFC 9403](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9403), EPUB 3.3 is also in the final stages of its recommended track. Is there time left to revisit this issue?

body:
As raised in https://github.com/w3c/epubcheck/issues/1481, there are rare occurrences where the value of the viewport meta is expressed with a fractional part.  The current definition, however, says the value must be a positive number, suggesting only positive integers are allowed.

We should probably make clear that decimal values are allowed but reading systems may ignore the fractional part.

title: Restriction on epub:type in svg is too strict

labels.name: Spec-EPUB3
labels.description: The issue affects the core EPUB 3.X Recommendation

labels.name: EPUB33

labels.name: Errata
labels.description: Item accepted as an official errata for one or several specs

labels.name: Change-Class-3
labels.description: Requested changes are of class 3 (per process)

body:
As reported in https://github.com/w3c/epubcheck/issues/1497, the current [restriction on epub:type in svg content documents](https://www.w3.org/TR/epub-33/#confreq-svg-structural-semantics) does not allow the attribute on `a` elements.

The definition of [renderable elements](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG2/render.html#TermRenderableElement) is probably a better alternative than the three categories listed.

(If the current three categories are kept, however, note that they link to the svg 1.1 specification so should be updated.)
